name: GNOME
full_name: Global Network of Optical Magnetometers for Exotic physics searches
summary: A worldwide atomic-magnetometer network searching for structures such as axionlike-field domain walls through correlated transients at multiple stations.
detection_principle: A hypothetical dark-matter domain wall passing Earth produces a pseudomagnetic field acting on atomic spins; GPS-synchronized stations search for signals with consistent propagation delays.

sites.name: Magnetometer network across Europe, North America, Asia, the Middle East and Australia
sites.location: Magnetometer network across Europe, North America, Asia, the Middle East and Australia

status.label: Experimental operation in the phase documented by the source
status.evidence: 2021 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

timeline.event: Search for topological defect dark matter with a global network of optical magnetometers

collaboration.name: GNOME Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

key_parameters.name: 2021 analysis
key_parameters.value: Approximately one month of continuous network data

results.summary: No statistically significant correlated signal; constraints were obtained for the adopted domain-wall model.

science_scope: Targets transient spin interactions from dark-matter topological defects; sensitivity depends on domain-wall thickness, encounter rate and coupling assumptions. It is not a detector at a single fixed geographic point.
